newsitem.title: INDIA: JM Mutual plans index fund to track BSE, NSE.
newsitem.headline: JM Mutual plans index fund to track BSE, NSE.

text.p: India's JM Mutual Fund said on Wednesday it would launch an index fund later this month.
The scheme will have two plans. The first will track the 50-share National Stock Exchange (NSE) index, the second will track the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index.
The money raised will be exclusively invested in shares tracked by the two indices, JM Fund officials said.
"Index funds are the flavour of the day in the western world," S.V. Prasad, president and chief executive of JM Capital Management Ltd, which manages the mutual funds, said.
JM Mutual manages 1.75 billion rupees in various schemes.
Other schemes on the anvil are JM Children Scheme (for parents to save money to provide for children's education), JM Pension Fund and JM Infrastructure Fund.
The pension and infrastructure funds are awaiting approvals from the ministry of finance, JM Mutual officials said.
